question: Does the descriptive onset-rate difference between zero-to-positive and positive-to-positive production persist within the same month and exact hour?
previous_evidence: 002: zero-to-positive onset rates 16/163 and 13/52 exceed positive-to-positive rates 102/2100 and 71/562, but hour composition differs and current production is posthoc
scope: Same valid Jan-Aug records and exact previous-hour eligibility as 002; exploratory maximum-of-four threshold 182; no deletions of zero values
common_support: Stratum retained for comparison only if both groups have at least one eligible record; quantify excluded denominators and onsets separately. No minimum-size tuning.
standardization: Within period, use pooled eligible exposure in each common-support stratum as a common weight for both group-specific onset rates; repeat using inverse within-period daily-profile frequency for exposure and onset totals
outputs: All pair records, per-stratum counts, raw and profile-weighted standardized rates, support retention and minimum cell sizes; no significance claims
interpretation: All comparisons use current production and are posthoc. Current positive production is held common, but unmeasured operating conditions, sparse cells, repeated profiles and measurement definitions remain unresolved.
decision: If association changes direction or magnitude with common support and standardization, revise the crude transition interpretation. Stop before a causal or operational claim; do not tune cutoffs or strata to recover a preferred result.
